body:
## What happened

A legs soreness entry logged against the Aug 14 workout never reached the server. The pod log for that whole session holds exactly one mutation:

```
DELETE /api/soreness/soreness-2026-08-15-logged-workout-2026-08-14-day1-… → 404
```

No `POST`. Saving with an empty muscle list meant "you cleared this entry", so it fired a DELETE, swallowed the 404 for a document that had never existed, and closed the editor as though it had saved.

## Three compounding faults

- **"Change workout" wiped the entry.** It reused the fresh-entry setup, so returning from the workout list emptied the muscles and reset the date to today — even when the same workout was re-picked. Reproduced; this is the one confirmed way to reach an empty list without touching it.
- **An empty save was a covert delete**, with no confirmation and no error.
- **An entry with no muscles could not be represented**, which is what made "empty" read as "deleted".

## Changes

- Re-attributing mid-edit keeps the date and muscles; only the attribution changes.
- An entry with no muscles is a real entry and draws its stripe — the `peak N` label just drops off.
- Deleting is its own **Delete entry** button, not a side effect of emptying a list.
- Stripe opacity no longer encodes severity: levels 3 and 5 rendered at 0.50 vs 0.64 against a dark ground, which is not a readable difference. Colour now means one thing — which workout.
- Source picker heading is a directive ("Select the workout that made you sore") rather than a question. It's a required step in a flow, not a conversational field.

## Verification

Driven in a real browser against the live data: empty save now POSTs and the stripe renders; re-picking a workout preserves date and muscles; the muscle-free test entry was removed from the database afterwards.
title: Stop a soreness save from silently deleting the entry
